item.title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.37016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter. Secondly, we study finite multitensor 2-categories, that is, finite linear 2-categories equipped with a monoidal structure for which every objects has duals. We extend several results about fusion 2-categories to our present setting. In particular, we investigate the properties of the 2-category of bimodules over a rigid algebra $\mathcal{A}$ in a finite tensor 2-category $\mathfrak{C}$. We show that, if $\mathfrak{C}$ has adjunctible projectives, then the 2-category of $\mathcal{A}$-$\mathcal{A}$-bimodules in $\mathfrak{C}$ is a finite multitensor 2-category. This construction provides many examples of finite tensor 2-categories. For instance, the Drinfeld center of a finite tensor 2-category with adjunctible projectives is a finite tensor 2-category.
item.dc:creator: Thibault D. D\'ecoppet, Mateusz Stroi\'nski, Tony Zorman

item.title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.36119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres. We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes supported on immersed curves. We prove that the topological category embeds into the geometric category in an essentially unique way. To define Lagrangian branes we develop a generalisation of the Chekanov--Eliashberg algebra incorporating dg-coefficients and wrapping along the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Daniil Mamaev

item.title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2610.36314v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex. As a main application, we obtain an intrinsic geometric explanation for the appearance of vanishing cycle data for perverse sheaves in a paracyclic variant of the Dold--Kan correspondence pioneered by Dwyer and Kan, at the same time lifting their equivalence to stable $\infty$-categories.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider

item.title: Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.36966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects. We establish compact generation and study the stronger requirement that every compact object admits a finitely presented cofibrant representative. We call objects with such representatives perfect. Under local coherence and the existence of enough projectives among the finitely presented objects, the finitely presented cofibrant objects form a Frobenius category whose stable category describes the perfect objects and whose idempotent completion recovers all compact objects. The relative $Q$-shaped setting, for suitable small categories $Q$, makes explicit how these finiteness properties depend on the choice of exact structure. The pure exact structure yields a compactly generated homotopy category, called the $Q$-shaped pure derived category. On the other hand, the split exact structure yields the $Q$-shaped homotopy category, which is compactly generated only in the pure semisimple case, analogously to the classical homotopy category of complexes. Finally, for acyclic $Q$ and for left artinian rings, we show that every compact object admits a strictly perfect representative. In particular, we establish that compact and perfect objects coincide, proving the conjecture of Holm and Jorgensen under these hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Anastasios Slaftsos

item.title: Re-framing the classification of ideals in noncommutative tensor triangular geometry
item.description: arXiv:2510.23767v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a 'pseudo-Hochster dual' of the noncommutative Balmer spectrum of a monoidal triangulated category classifies its semiprime thick tensor ideals. This extends Balmer's classification of radical thick tensor ideals to noncommutative tensor triangular geometry. To achieve this, we utilize the notion of support data for lattices and frames, under which the classification follows via Stone duality. We also give a characterization for when the noncommutative Balmer spectrum behaves as it does in tensor triangular geometry, that is, when it is a spectral space with quasi-compact opens given by complements of supports. Finally, we show that rigid centrally generated monoidal triangulated categories satisfy this property, and we answer a question posed by Negron--Pevtsova regarding classification of one-sided tensor ideals via cohomological support.
item.dc:creator: Timothy De Deyn, Sam K. Miller

item.title: Some notes on tensor triangular geometry
item.description: arXiv:2602.08480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: These are notes from the lectures I gave at the Oberwolfach seminar `Tensor Triangular Geometry and Interactions' which was held in October 2025. The aim of these notes is to give an introduction to tensor triangular geometry, for both small and large categories, through the lens of lattice theory. We do not try to be exhaustive and this is reflected in both the content and the bibliography. For instance we are quite light on triangulated preliminaries, especially for compactly generated categories. The first three sections treat the essentially small case and conclude with a tensor triangular proof of Thomason's theorem computing the spectrum of the perfect complexes on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The last section treats the compactly generated case. This final section is somewhat experimental and contains some new thoughts.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stevenson

item.title: Limit Computation Over Posets via Minimal Initial Functors
item.description: arXiv:2601.00209v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is well known that limits can be computed by restricting along an initial functor, and that this often simplifies limit computation. We systematically study the algorithmic implications of this idea for diagrams indexed by a poset. We say an initial functor $F\colon C\to D$ with $C$ small is minimal if the sets of objects and morphisms of $C$ each have minimum cardinality, among the sources of all initial functors with target $D$. For $Q$ a finite poset or $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ an interval (i.e., a convex, connected subposet), we describe all minimal initial functors $F\colon P\to Q$. In particular, we show that such $F$ is always a subposet inclusion, up to isomorphism. We give efficient algorithms to compute a choice of minimal initial functor. In the case that $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ is an interval, we give asymptotically optimal bounds on $|\hom P|$, the number of relations in $P$ (including identities), in terms of the number $n$ of minima of $Q$: We show that $|\hom P|=\Theta(n)$ for $d\leq 3$, and $|\hom P|=\Theta(n^2)$ for $d>3$. We apply these results to give new bounds on the cost of computing $\lim G$ for a functor $G \colon Q\to \mathbf{Vec}$ valued in vector spaces. For $Q$ connected, we also give new bounds on the cost of computing the generalized rank of $G$ (i.e., the rank of the induced map $\lim G\to \operatorname{colim} G$), which is of interest in topological data analysis.
item.dc:creator: Tamal K. Dey, Michael Lesnick
